```python
# Treat each statement as a fact; no rules connect species to colors.
facts = {
    ("Lily", "species", "lion"),
    ("Lily", "color", "yellow"),
    ("Julius", "species", "lion"),
    ("Julius", "color", "gray"),
    ("Brian", "species", "swan"),
    ("Brian", "color", "green"),
    ("Bernhard", "species", "rhino"),
    ("Bernhard", "color", "yellow"),
    ("Greg", "species", "swan"),
}

greg_colors = sorted(
    value for subject, predicate, value in facts
    if subject == "Greg" and predicate == "color"
)

# Two consistent extensions demonstrate that the context does not
# uniquely determine Greg's color.
extensions = [
    facts | {("Greg", "color", "green")},
    facts | {("Greg", "color", "yellow")},
]
consistent = all(
    facts <= model
    and all(
        len({v for s, p, v in model if s == name and p == "color"}) <= 1
        for name in {s for s, _, _ in model}
    )
    for model in extensions
)

print("Explicit colors of Greg:", greg_colors)
print("Consistent alternative colors: green, yellow")
print("Expected answer: Greg's color is not specified.")
print("CHECK PASS" if not greg_colors and consistent else "CHECK FAIL")
```
